title: Finite synthesis TSVD with explicit Gram and synthesis cutoffs
summary: For any finite synthesis map, including dependent columns, a Gram cutoff lambda>epsilon gives error <=inf_z(||f-Tz||+sqrt(epsilon)||z||); moment noise adds ||e||/sqrt(epsilon).
conditions: Complex or real Hilbert space; finite linear synthesis T; exact adjoint and G=T*T.
epsilon>0 is an absolute Gram eigenvalue cutoff, with equality discarded.
Krein transfer requires fixed c>0, s=2 or4, f and every column in the genuine D(Kc^(s/2)).
scope: Finite projection and noise estimates. No frame or infinite convergence assumption. Original nonaffine sparse p_n are not valid s=4 columns.
content: Let G v_j=lambda_j v_j and u_j=T v_j/sqrt(lambda_j) for positive lambda_j. Then P_epsilon=T G_epsilon^dagger T*=sum_(lambda_j>epsilon)<.,u_j>u_j is an orthogonal projection. The discarded synthesis part has norm squared sum_(0<lambda_j<=epsilon)lambda_j|<z,v_j>|^2<=epsilon||z||^2. Decompose f-P_epsilon f=(I-P_epsilon)(f-Tz)+(I-P_epsilon)Tz to obtain the bound. If y=T*f+e, ||T G_epsilon^dagger e||<=epsilon^(-1/2)||e||. A synthesis singular-value cutoff sigma>tau is instead epsilon=tau^2; a relative Gram cutoff rho||G|| has penalty sqrt(rho)||T||||z||. The full theorem, coefficient estimate, zero-rank cases and conditional Hc transfer are in note02. A-H sigma_n denotes singular values of G_N, not T_N.
